correctness.rationale: For every support graph H, open-neighborhood traces are precisely two-vertex edge cuts of H. Any center has zero, one, or two endpoints in H, hence two fresh ambient vertices exhaust all possibilities. Complete edge-extension induction enumerates 1,2,5,11,26 unlabeled nonisolated graphs with 1–5 edges; the independent standard-library certificate checks their entire cut repertoires, identifies exactly ten admissible types of sizes 1–4, and excludes every five-edge type. Heredity rules out larger supports. Dividing labelled embeddings by graph automorphism orders yields all coefficients and correct small-order restrictions. Independent labelled brute force for n=2,...,10 and motif counts for n=2,...,12 reproduce the theorem. The universal statement follows from the exhaustive finite reduction, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The exact all-order shattering polynomial is a natural finer invariant of the canonical Johnson graph family, not just a cardinality bound. The theorem describes precisely which graph motifs contribute, the sharp ambient-order appearance of each, and quantitative rarity of shattered triples and quadruples among random supports (12/n and 48/n²). The coefficientwise counts are not determined by the known VC-dimension threshold; the four-support count is 2625 already at n=7. The result is mathematically motivated by NIP/VC-density and structural tameness, with no unsupported claim to extending the general Johnson bound.
